In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of whether the Open Access movement is a global trend or whether it is a movement that is confined to certain geographical regions.
the development of indicators to monitor the adoption of Open Access policies and practices in universities worldwide.
the following questions: How do we measure the OA penetration of a university's output? What are the challenges in measuring this? What are the limitations? How can we move forward?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the current data is not yet mature enough to provide a clear picture of the state of OA penetration at universities worldwide.
the implementation of OA policies is not enough to guarantee the adoption of an OA culture in universities.
the Open Access penetration of the global academic output is still low.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Open Access is a growing phenomenon worldwide, but there are still many challenges to be addressed to reach the goal of a fully Open Science culture.
the OA coverage of universities is still very heterogeneous and that the majority of the universities worldwide still have to improve the OA coverage of their output.
OA penetration is still very limited in most universities worldwide, and that there is an urgent need to develop indicators and policies that support the transition to Open Science.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the OA penetration in the scientific community is still very low.
the OA coverage of research output is still limited.

OA penetration is not a simple indicator to track and that there are still many challenges ahead for researchers, institutions, publishers and policy makers to reach a more sustainable, equitable and transparent research system.
